name: Erlotinib
route_note: oral tablet once daily on an empty stomach
originator: Pfizer (discovered), developed by OSI Pharmaceuticals with Genentech and Roche

discovery.note: A quinazoline EGFR inhibitor; rights were divested to OSI when Pfizer merged with Warner-Lambert in 2000.

tagline: Reversible EGFR inhibitor for EGFR-mutant lung cancer and pancreatic cancer
summary: Erlotinib is an oral reversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It was first approved after it modestly improved survival in unselected previously treated lung cancer, and is now used mainly as first-line therapy for EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer; it is also approved with gemcitabine for pancreatic cancer.
mechanism: Erlotinib competes with ATP at the EGFR intracellular kinase domain, inhibiting receptor autophosphorylation and downstream MAPK and PI3K–AKT signalling.

Tumours with exon 19 deletions or L858R mutations are highly sensitive; the T790M mutation confers acquired resistance. EGFR inhibition in skin and gut causes the characteristic acneiform rash and diarrhoea, and rash severity has been associated with benefit.
uses: First-line, maintenance or subsequent treatment of metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation
Locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer with gemcitabine

history.title: OSI rights
history.detail: Erlotinib rights pass to OSI Pharmaceuticals, which partners with Genentech and Roche.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: BR.21 shows a survival benefit in previously treated NSCLC; approved as Tarceva.

history.title: Pancreatic cancer
history.detail: Approved with gemcitabine for pancreatic cancer (PA.3).

history.title: EURTAC
history.detail: Erlotinib beats chemotherapy first-line in European EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

history.title: Companion diagnostic
history.detail: FDA approves first-line use in EGFR-mutant NSCLC with the cobas EGFR mutation test.

history.title: Label narrowed
history.detail: Maintenance and second-line use limited to EGFR-mutant tumours after IUNO trial.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A4, partly CYP1A2; smoking induces clearance

facts: Smokers clear erlotinib faster because tobacco smoke induces CYP1A2, lowering drug exposure.
